rest of my life and if you told me I'd be doing that 27 years later I'll make there's no chance in hell uh I'll be doing this I'm going to do something else um uh and here I am 27 years later loving it more than I've ever loved it and um that's how it that's how it started yeah thrown yeah I thrown in there and then they kind of gave me better and better players and I've just managed to you know get a couple results with them and that's how kind of it started but it was a complete fluke and I think uh yeah I think product of circumstance yeah that's um that's an incredible story in itself let's rewind to 1996 you started working with a young Andy Roddick what are your memories of that experience and how did it come about yeah so I actually was back in South Africa on vacation and uh John at this stage now the Everett Academy had bought out Robert Sigourso and Colin Bassett when I bought them out but they took a majority share I think 55% or something right and I've got a call from John I've been working for John for like a year or maybe eight months and he goes I've got this kid coming in he's based at Saddlebrook uh his name's Andy Roddick I'm like okay I'm gonna I've heard the name I don't know much I'm at bearing mind at this stage I'm like two years max into coaching still a complete rookie really don't know anything and um and he goes yeah I need you to uh coach him in the morning every morning for hour and a

half before school and then I need you to put him in the academy program and uh you know this kid's a high profile player I'm like okay well looking back I was probably a little bit naive because he was a high profile player and it was a great opportunity but because I was so naive and so ignorant it didn't affect me at all I was just gonna come in with my way or the highway which made us to have a lot of arguments with what is kind of crazy and I talk about this often is how he actually kind of trusted me and how um how his parents trusted me because he'd been around a lot of good coaches a lot at 14 years old and that's when I started him when he was 14 years old I started with him I think it was mid-February in 1996 and how that even came about actually I guess John must have told them something that made them buy into the fact that made credentials anyway so we started with that we got along great I mean he's um he's a firecracker he's like he's charismatic he's incredibly competitive he sends a humor as you know from interviews is off the charts yeah it's amazing sometimes yeah when I get bought bought I listen to his interviews I remember him listening to one in in Shanghai and uh I don't know somebody interviewed him and said he said something to him and he goes well I don't know what match you are watching but that wasn't the match that I played so you know really really funny guy anyway we got along well and um you know

we spent three years together and uh uh eventually I went one-on-one with him after my tenure at Everett's ended and um yeah we went one-on-one and and all I knew was that I didn't know anything I knew I knew nothing uh in the grand scheme of things and yeah his brother John was a very good player and his parents had a self-admittedly made mistakes by interesting people that didn't have they knew that the only thing that I cared about was actually you know getting getting Andy to be the best he can be even though when I look back now wow I knew very very little I did know to look out um you know look at the game look at the game and see what the best players were doing with potentially the game was going I did know that he was the type of player that if I put him in a situation where he was not the best player in other words take him to tournaments where the other guys were better you'd figure out pretty quickly what needed to be done but because he was such a good competitor he a lot of times found out how to win anyway um but that was the biggest thing is that I learned on the job with him and it was pretty cool and I'm actually incredibly fortunate that his parents entrusted me to kind of do that but uh yeah I didn't come in I didn't come out of the gates with a lot of knowledge it was like on the job learning with him yeah they must have sensed your skill and your ability to develop him or they would have been out of there
